name: GoodStudent
label: Good student status
description: Whether the driver qualifies as a good student (GPA ≥ 3.0 or equivalent).
mechanism: GoodStudent is a binary indicator jointly determined by Age (primarily Adolescent/young Adult) and SocioEcon (academic performance correlates with socioeconomic resources and parental investment). It serves as a risk proxy that feeds RiskAversion: good students are empirically more likely to be Cautious or Normal drivers. Not a vehicle or cost node.

name: Age
label: Driver age group
description: Driver's age bracket; the most broadly connected demographic root node.
mechanism: Root node with no modeled parents. Age has three direct downstream effects: GoodStudent (Adolescent most eligible), SeniorTrain (Senior-only intervention), and DrivingSkill (Adolescent and Senior both have elevated SubStandard probability due to inexperience and age-related decline respectively). Age is the most connected root node in the driver sub-network.

name: SocioEcon
label: Socio-economic status
description: Household socio-economic tier; shapes vehicle and neighbourhood choices.
mechanism: Root node with no modeled parents. SocioEcon is the primary economic constraint variable: it determines vehicle tier (MakeModel), residential location (HomeBase), and contributes to GoodStudent. Wealthy drivers drive Luxury/SuperLuxury vehicles in Secure/Suburb areas; Prole drivers drive Economy vehicles in City/Rural areas. SocioEcon is the root that connects vehicle quality to neighbourhood theft risk.

name: RiskAversion
label: Risk aversion tendency
description: Dispositional risk attitude; primary behavioural input to driving quality.
mechanism: RiskAversion is influenced by GoodStudent (good students trend Cautious). It is the behavioural component of DrivQuality (interacting with DrivingSkill) and also drives Mileage exposure (risk-seeking drivers drive more). It is the key node bridging demographic background and accident risk: high risk aversion can partly compensate for low driving skill, and vice versa.

name: VehicleYear
label: Vehicle model year
description: Vehicle recency; proxy for safety technology availability.
mechanism: Root node. VehicleYear is the temporal technology proxy: Current vehicles have substantially higher probability of having Antilock brakes, Airbags, and AntiTheft systems than older vehicles. It also contributes to CarValue (depreciation means older vehicles are worth less). VehicleYear is the key root node connecting model-year to three downstream safety and value nodes.

name: ThisCarDam
label: Damage to insured car
description: Physical damage severity to the insured vehicle.
mechanism: ThisCarDam is jointly determined by Accident severity (more severe accident → more damage) and RuggedAuto (structural protection moderates damage given accident severity). The interaction is multiplicative: Accident=Severe + RuggedAuto=EggShell → near-certain Severe damage; Accident=Mild + RuggedAuto=Tank → likely None or Mild. ThisCarDam directly drives ThisCarCost.

name: RuggedAuto
label: Vehicle structural ruggedness
description: Structural crashworthiness category; moderates accident-to-damage translation.
mechanism: RuggedAuto is determined by MakeModel: SportsCar/Economy → EggShell (lightweight, poor crash structure); FamilySedan → Football (average); Luxury/SuperLuxury → Tank (high-strength steel, crumple zones). RuggedAuto moderates ThisCarDam and jointly determines Cushioning (with Airbag). It is the primary vehicle-side damage moderation node.

name: Accident
label: Accident severity
description: Overall accident severity; the central loss event node.
mechanism: Accident is the central hub of the loss sub-network. It is determined by DrivQuality (proximate behavioural cause), Mileage (exposure), Antilock (active safety mitigation), and OtherCar (multi-vehicle amplification of severity). It simultaneously drives ThisCarDam (own vehicle), OtherCarCost (third-party), and MedCost (injuries). Accident is the highest-fanout outcome node in the network.

name: MakeModel
label: Car make/model class
description: Vehicle class; the primary vehicle-side root determining all vehicle attributes.
mechanism: MakeModel is determined by SocioEcon. It is the most connected vehicle node: it determines RuggedAuto (crash structure), CarValue (market price), Antilock availability, Airbag availability, and indirectly AntiTheft. MakeModel is the key common cause for all vehicle attribute nodes, making it a critical fork in the vehicle sub-network.

name: DrivQuality
label: Driving quality
description: Synthesized driving performance; the proximate cause of accident risk.
mechanism: DrivQuality integrates DrivingSkill (technical competency) and RiskAversion (behavioural disposition). The interaction is approximately multiplicative: Expert skill + Cautious attitude → Excellent; SubStandard skill + Psychopath attitude → Poor (certain). A skilled but reckless driver (Expert + Adventurous) tends toward Normal, not Excellent. DrivQuality is the direct proximate cause of Accident severity, rendering Accident conditionally independent of DrivingSkill and RiskAversion given DrivQuality.

name: Mileage
label: Annual mileage bucket
description: Annual miles driven; pure exposure multiplier on accident risk.
mechanism: Mileage is influenced by RiskAversion (risk-seeking drivers drive more). It functions as an exposure variable: holding DrivQuality constant, higher mileage increases accident probability proportionally to kilometres at risk. Domino represents extreme mileage (commercial or rideshare level, ~100k+ miles/year). Mileage also affects OtherCar probability (more driving in dense areas).

name: Antilock
label: Antilock braking system (ABS)
description: ABS presence; active safety system reducing accident severity.
mechanism: Antilock is determined by MakeModel (standard on Luxury/SuperLuxury) and VehicleYear (Current vehicles). When True, ABS directly reduces P(Accident=Severe or Moderate) by maintaining steering control during hard braking. It is conditionally independent of driver profile nodes given MakeModel and VehicleYear.

name: DrivingSkill
label: Driver skill level
description: Technical driving competency; the skill component of driving quality.
mechanism: DrivingSkill is determined by three inputs: Age (inexperience in Adolescents, decline in Seniors), SeniorTrain (completed training improves Senior skill), and DrivHist (more prior incidents → lower skill rating). DrivingSkill feeds DrivQuality as the technical component, interacting with RiskAversion. Given DrivQuality, DrivingSkill is conditionally independent of Accident.

name: SeniorTrain
label: Senior driver training
description: Completion of senior driver refresher program; Age-conditional intervention.
mechanism: SeniorTrain is available only to Senior-age drivers (Age=Senior prerequisite). When True, it improves DrivingSkill. It is a targeted intervention node: its effect is zero for non-Seniors (P(SeniorTrain=True | Age=Adolescent or Adult) ≈ 0). This makes SeniorTrain a key node for policy interventions targeting the Senior segment.

name: ThisCarCost
label: Insured car claim cost
description: Total financial cost for the insured vehicle (repair or total loss).
mechanism: ThisCarCost is determined by two independent pathways: (1) damage pathway: ThisCarDam × CarValue (damage severity × replacement cost basis); (2) theft pathway: Theft × CarValue (total loss value). Both pathways interact through CarValue, making CarValue the key moderating variable for all this-car financial outcomes. ThisCarCost feeds PropCost.

name: Theft
label: Vehicle theft
description: Whether the insured vehicle was stolen.
mechanism: Theft probability is determined by three factors: CarValue (more valuable cars more targeted), HomeBase (City highest crime; Secure lowest), and AntiTheft (deterrence reduces probability). These combine as: attractive target (CarValue) × access opportunity (HomeBase) × deterrence (AntiTheft). Theft feeds ThisCarCost as a total-loss pathway independent of the accident pathway.

name: CarValue
label: Insured car value
description: Market value of the insured vehicle; the financial scale parameter for all property costs.
mechanism: CarValue is determined by MakeModel (primary value driver: SuperLuxury → Million; Economy → FiveThou) and VehicleYear (Current → higher value due to no depreciation). CarValue is a common cause of two important downstream nodes: Theft (attractive target) and ThisCarCost (replacement cost ceiling). It is the financial scale moderator for all property-related costs.

name: HomeBase
label: Home neighbourhood type
description: Residential neighbourhood type; ambient risk environment.
mechanism: HomeBase is determined by SocioEcon (Wealthy → Secure; Prole → City primarily). It influences two downstream nodes: Theft (City has highest crime density) and OtherCar (City traffic density increases multi-vehicle collision probability). HomeBase is the bridge node between socio-economic status and environmental risk.

name: AntiTheft
label: Anti-theft system
description: Anti-theft device; primary deterrent reducing theft probability.
mechanism: AntiTheft presence is determined by MakeModel (standard on Luxury/SuperLuxury) and VehicleYear (Current vehicles more likely equipped). AntiTheft has a single downstream effect: directly reducing Theft probability. It has no effect on accident severity, driving quality, or any cost node other than through Theft.

name: PropCost
label: Proportional cost comparison
description: Relative cost summary comparing insured-car to other-car costs.
mechanism: PropCost aggregates ThisCarCost and OtherCarCost into a comparative cost ratio used for policy pricing and claim reserve estimation. It is a terminal aggregation leaf — the highest-level cost summary node in the network with no downstream effects.

name: OtherCarCost
label: Other car claim cost
description: Third-party vehicle cost; liability cost for the other vehicle.
mechanism: OtherCarCost is determined by Accident severity and OtherCar (prerequisite: if OtherCar=False, OtherCarCost=Thousand with near-certainty). Severe multi-vehicle accidents with an involved third party (OtherCar=True) produce the highest OtherCarCost. OtherCarCost feeds PropCost.

name: OtherCar
label: Other vehicle involved
description: Whether a second vehicle participates in the incident.
mechanism: OtherCar is influenced by HomeBase (City traffic density increases multi-vehicle collision probability) and Mileage (more driving exposure increases encounter probability). OtherCar=True both amplifies Accident severity (multi-vehicle crashes are more severe) and is the prerequisite for OtherCarCost. This creates a v-structure at Accident (DrivQuality → Accident ← OtherCar) that is important for explaining-away inference.

name: MedCost
label: Medical treatment cost
description: Medical cost of accident-related injuries.
mechanism: MedCost is jointly determined by Accident severity (more severe accident → more injuries) and Cushioning quality (Poor cushioning amplifies injury given accident). These interact multiplicatively: Severe accident + Poor cushioning → near-certain HundredThou/Million costs; Mild accident + Excellent cushioning → Thousand. MedCost feeds ILiCost.

name: Cushioning
label: Occupant cushioning quality
description: Integrated occupant protection quality; modulates injury severity given accident.
mechanism: Cushioning is determined by Airbag (primary active protection component) and RuggedAuto (structural passive protection). The two inputs interact: Airbag=True + RuggedAuto=Tank → almost certainly Excellent; Airbag=False + RuggedAuto=EggShell → almost certainly Poor. Cushioning then moderates how Accident severity translates into MedCost.

name: Airbag
label: Airbag present
description: Airbag availability; primary active occupant protection system.
mechanism: Airbag is determined by MakeModel (standard on Luxury/SuperLuxury; rare on older Economy) and VehicleYear (Current vehicles standard-equipped post-1998 mandate). Airbag is the dominant input to Cushioning quality; its presence reduces MedCost through improved Cushioning. Given MakeModel and VehicleYear, Airbag is conditionally independent of all driver profile nodes.

name: ILiCost
label: Injury / liability cost
description: Total injury and legal liability cost; terminal liability cost leaf.
mechanism: ILiCost aggregates MedCost (direct injury costs) into a total injury-and-liability bucket that incorporates third-party bodily injury liability, legal defence costs, and pain-and-suffering settlements. It is a terminal leaf node with no downstream effects in the model.

name: DrivHist
label: Prior driving incidents
description: Bucketed count of prior at-fault accidents or moving violations.
mechanism: Root node with no modeled parents. DrivHist is a historical record that directly informs DrivingSkill: Many incidents → SubStandard skill much more probable. It is also the primary observable actuarial risk indicator, as it is the most reliable predictor of future claims. DrivHist is causally upstream of DrivingSkill only — it does not directly affect RiskAversion or any vehicle node.
